## Barry fixtures

Repositories generated with Barry, and what a correct validator must conclude from each.

### M0

#### `m0-minimal-valid`: Minimal valid repository: TA, one CA, one ROA

The smallest repository that exercises a full chain: a trust anchor that
certifies one CA, which issues one ROA. Each publication point has the CRL
and manifest Barry generates. Nothing is overridden, so every object is
correct.

In M0 it proves the fixture pipeline works end to end: descriptor,
generation, metadata check, catalog and test helper. In later milestones
it is the positive baseline: every stage of the validator must accept it
and produce exactly one VRP. Invalid fixtures should differ from it in
one field, so a rejection can be traced to that one change.

- **Expected:** valid
- **RFC:** [6481 §2](../rfc/rfc6481.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6481.html#section-2)), [8630 §2.2](../rfc/rfc8630.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8630.html#section-2.2)), [6487 §4](../rfc/rfc6487.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6487.html#section-4)), [9286 §4](../rfc/rfc9286.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9286.html#section-4)), [9582 §4](../rfc/rfc9582.txt) ([html](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9582.html#section-4))
- **Files:** [descriptor](../../test/fixtures/barry/m0-minimal-valid/case.repo) · [metadata](../../test/fixtures/barry/m0-minimal-valid/case.exs) · [rsync tree](../../test/fixtures/barry/m0-minimal-valid/rsync)

## Unit tests

Grouped by test module. Doctests are not listed: they are documented by the function docs they come from.

### `Lumina.FixturesMetadataTest`

[test/fixtures_metadata_test.exs](../../test/fixtures_metadata_test.exs)

Enforces that every Barry fixture documents why it exists, which RFC
sections it checks and what a validator must conclude from it, and that
its generated output is present. See doc/testing.md.

- every fixture has complete metadata and generated output

### `Lumina.Fixtures.M0MinimalValidTest`

[test/lumina/fixtures/m0_minimal_valid_test.exs](../../test/lumina/fixtures/m0_minimal_valid_test.exs)

Checks that the m0-minimal-valid fixture loads and contains the files Barry
should produce for a TA -> CA -> ROA tree. This proves the fixture
pipeline works end to end (descriptor, generation, metadata, test helper)
before any object is decoded. Decoding and validation start in M1.

- loads with its metadata
- the rsync tree contains exactly the expected objects, each non-empty and readable
- RPKI objects are DER: each file starts with a SEQUENCE tag
- the TAL's rsync URI points to the trust anchor certificate in the tree
- the TAL's public key is base64 that decodes to a DER SEQUENCE
- the RRDP files are present

### `LuminaTest`

[test/lumina_test.exs](../../test/lumina_test.exs)

Smoke test for the application module: the project builds and reports
its version.

- version/0 matches the version in mix.exs

### `Mix.Lumina.CatalogTest`

[test/mix/lumina/catalog_test.exs](../../test/mix/lumina/catalog_test.exs)

Tests rendering of doc/tests/CATALOG.md: content, grouping, order, links
and determinism. The catalog is committed and checked in CI, so output
must not depend on input order.

- says so when there are no fixtures or unit tests
- marks the file as generated
- groups by milestone and sorts by id within a milestone
- an entry shows the rationale, expected outcome, RFC links and files
- a valid fixture says so
- links are relative to where the catalog is written
- *unit tests:* lists each test module with its moduledoc, file and tests, in file order
- *unit tests:* shows the describe block, RFC references and doc tag of a test
- *unit tests:* says so for a module with only doctests
- *unit tests:* leaves out helper modules that don't use ExUnit.Case
- rendering is deterministic regardless of input order

### `Mix.Lumina.FixturesTest`

[test/mix/lumina/fixtures_test.exs](../../test/mix/lumina/fixtures_test.exs)

Tests the fixture metadata check: every way a fixture can be incomplete
or wrong must be reported, and case.exs must be read as data without
running any code in it. Fixtures are built in temporary directories.

- a complete fixture passes
- a valid fixture with Barry overrides passes
- *required metadata:* a missing rationale fails
- *required metadata:* a blank rationale fails
- *required metadata:* a missing RFC reference fails
- *required metadata:* an empty RFC list fails
- *required metadata:* an invalid RFC reference fails
- *required metadata:* a missing expected outcome fails
- *required metadata:* a malformed expected outcome fails
- *required metadata:* a rejected object that isn't in the rsync tree fails
- *required metadata:* an id that doesn't match the folder fails
- *required metadata:* an id that doesn't start with the milestone fails
- *required metadata:* an unknown milestone fails
- *required metadata:* an unknown key fails
- *required metadata:* bad Barry options fail
- *case.exs is data, not code:* function calls are rejected without being run
- *case.exs is data, not code:* string interpolation is rejected
- *case.exs is data, not code:* metadata that is not a map is rejected
- *case.exs is data, not code:* unparseable metadata is rejected
- *files:* a missing case.exs fails
- *files:* a missing descriptor fails
- *files:* missing generated output fails and says how to fix it
- load_all/2 returns passing fixtures and every problem

### `Mix.Lumina.RFCTest`

[test/mix/lumina/rfc_test.exs](../../test/mix/lumina/rfc_test.exs)

Tests RFC reference parsing and the section index built from doc/rfc.
These decide whether a test or fixture's RFC citation is accepted, so a
bug here would let wrong citations through or reject correct ones.

- *parse/1:* accepts numbered sections, appendices and appendix subsections
- *parse/1:* rejects malformed references
- *parse/1:* rejects values that are not strings
- *load_library/1:* loads every RFC in doc/rfc
- *load_library/1:* finds numbered sections, appendices and appendix subsections
- *load_library/1:* every RFC in the library has a section 1
- *validate/2:* accepts a reference to an existing section
- *validate/2:* rejects an RFC that is not in the library
- *validate/2:* rejects a section that does not exist
- *validate/2:* passes on parse errors

### `Mix.Lumina.TestScannerTest`

[test/mix/lumina/test_scanner_test.exs](../../test/mix/lumina/test_scanner_test.exs)

Tests the static test scanner that drives the RFC reference check, the
unit-test documentation check and the unit-test section of the catalog.
Sample test files are given as source strings and parsed, never compiled.

- *RFC references:* collects @tag, @describetag and @moduletag references, outermost first
- *RFC references:* @tag applies only to the next test
- *RFC references:* @describetag does not leak out of its describe block
- *RFC references:* reports tags whose value is not a literal string or list of strings
- *RFC references:* validate_refs/2 returns one problem per invalid reference, naming the test
- *modules and tests:* collects every test with its module, describe block and ExUnit name
- *modules and tests:* reads @moduledoc from a string, a heredoc, a ~S sigil, or false
- *modules and tests:* records whether a module uses ExUnit.Case
- *modules and tests:* names nested modules after their parent
- *modules and tests:* @tag doc: is attached to the next test only
- *modules and tests:* rejects doc: that is blank, not a literal, or not on @tag
- *modules and tests:* reports files that cannot be parsed
- *check_docs/1:* passes a documented module
- *check_docs/1:* fails a test module without @moduledoc
- *check_docs/1:* fails a test module with @moduledoc false
- *check_docs/1:* fails a blank @moduledoc
- *check_docs/1:* fails a blank test name
- *check_docs/1:* ignores helper modules that don't use ExUnit.Case

### `Lumina.TestDocsTest`

[test/test_docs_test.exs](../../test/test_docs_test.exs)

Enforces the rule that every unit test is documented (doc/testing.md):
every test module has a @moduledoc and every test a non-blank name. It
also checks that the static scanner behind the test catalog sees exactly
the tests ExUnit runs, so the catalog can't silently miss one.

- every test module has a @moduledoc and every test a name
- the scanner finds exactly the tests ExUnit runs, in every loaded test module
  When run with the whole suite, this covers every test module. When a
  single file is run, it covers the modules ExUnit loaded for that run.
  Doctests are excluded: they are documented by the function docs they
  come from.
